notes:
With the assistant installed and a graphics card, the companion can now word some of its comments itself, from counts only, never your text. If a line comes back too long, in the wrong language or with a number it made up, it uses its own written line instead.

Talking to the companion now keeps the thread: ask about a comment it just made and it answers about that comment, in its own voice, in your language.

The companion and the assistant panel can suggest a synonym that fits the sentence, reword a sentence a check flagged, or shorten the text you selected. You see the before and after, and nothing changes until you choose Apply. At «Ask me before each change» or «Allow changes» the change is saved in a snapshot first and listed in the activity log, where one click undoes it; at «Nothing» or «Read only» it tells you which setting allows it.

Two new companions join Ogam: Cob, a red squirrel who stores your words like nuts for winter, and Quoth, a raven in round glasses with a dry sense of humour about herself. Each has twelve expressions and her own lines in English and Spanish.

Settings → Companion now shows the whole cast before you download anything, with a portrait, a sample line and the download size. Each character installs on its own, and switching between them happens at once.

Three more companions join the cast: Fintan, a curious salmon in a jar of well water who wonders what comes next in your story; Maud, a lighthouse keeper who logs your pace once you set a target; and Dormy, a sleepy hazel dormouse whose jokes are always on himself. Pick one in Settings → Companion.

Now and then the companion offers a next step: a snapshot after a long stretch of revising, or a search when you keep opening the same Story Bible entry. Nothing happens until you click, and a snapshot still asks first.

«Presence only» in Settings → Companion keeps your companion reacting to your work without ever commenting. Installed companions offer an Update when a new version of their pack is out.

macOS: Corylus is not notarized yet, so Gatekeeper may say the app cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified. Right-click (or Control-click) Corylus.app, choose Open, then Open again. Only needed once per downloaded copy.
